findings.title: Neighbor ordering is unspecified across spatial implementations
findings.description: The query contract does not define result ordering. Different orders from brute-force and spatial-hash implementations can change floating-point force sums, conflicting with the slice plan’s requirement that slice 105 preserve behavioral output and determinism. Define a canonical neighbor order and require both implementations to return it.

findings.title: Neighbor interface conflicts with the bulk hot-path goal
findings.description: The design queries one agent at a time and passes a dynamically allocated list of per-agent arrays to each bulk force. The architecture calls for bulk array inputs without Python-level per-agent branching or dynamic allocation in the hot loop for eventual GPU offload. Define a batch-oriented neighbor representation and query contract, while retaining the brute-force implementation as the initial provider.

findings.title: Per-agent force path is both ambiguous and extra scope
findings.description: The document says the tick prefers bulk forces when available and requires testing both protocol paths, but its signature accepts only `list[BulkForce]`. It does not specify registration or dispatch for per-agent forces. Cut the separate production `Force` path and use bulk placeholder forces; the slice plan requires basic integration, not two force dispatch mechanisms.

findings.title: Performance target is not restated for the affected path
findings.description: The design targets hundreds of agents without restating the parent architecture’s goal of **tens of thousands of agents at full behavioral fidelity on one CPU process**. State that target and distinguish it from the deliberately limited brute-force implementation; the slice plan assigns spatial optimization to slice 105.

findings.title: Full pairwise distance storage adds avoidable quadratic memory
findings.description: Precomputing all pairwise distances on every build adds quadratic storage even when only a small subset is active, while queries still cost O(n). Use a simpler on-demand brute-force distance calculation for active queries and leave spatial indexing optimization to slice 105.
